setupSteps: Warm up first. 2 to 3 minutes of gentle movement (a few cat-cows, shoulder rolls, easy knee hugs) or do the pose after other poses. Never twist cold.
Floor. Flat mat or carpet; avoid slippery tiles.
Sit on a prop. Place a folded blanket or firm cushion about 5 to 10 cm thick (est.) under the sitting bones. Raising the hips makes it easier to sit tall and keep the spine long.

Legs, easy version. Either (a) sit cross-legged (Sukhasana) with the shins loosely crossed, or (b) extend the bottom leg straight and place the other foot flat outside it. Use whichever lets you sit tall without the lower back rounding.

Legs, standard version. From a seated position with the legs forward (Dandasana), bend one knee and place that foot flat outside the opposite thigh or knee. The other leg stays straight, or is folded in with the foot near the opposite hip.
Sit tall. Press both sitting bones down evenly; lengthen the spine up; hands on the floor beside you.
Clothing. Stretchy pants and a fitted top so the camera sees the shoulder line and hip line; no tight jeans.
Camera. Phone at about chest height on a stool or shelf (about 60 to 90 cm, est.), about 2 m in front, so the whole body from head to knees is in frame (see sections 11 and 12).

steps.title: Sit tall
steps.action: sit on the blanket, legs forward or crossed, spine long, hands by the hips.
steps.feel: sitting bones pressing down, crown of the head lifting.

steps.title: Set the legs
steps.action: for the standard version, bend the right knee and place the right foot flat outside the left thigh; keep the left leg straight. For the easy version, cross the legs loosely.
steps.feel: both sitting bones still heavy and level.

steps.title: Place the hands
steps.action: set the right hand on the floor behind you, fingers pointing away, a hand-width behind the hips. Hook the left elbow outside the right knee, or rest the left hand on the knee.
steps.feel: arms supporting; shoulders away from the ears.

steps.title: Lengthen on an in-breath
steps.action: breathe in and lift the spine, pressing the back hand into the floor to grow taller.
steps.feel: the ribs lifting away from the hips; the spine long, not slumped.

steps.title: Twist on the out-breath
steps.action: breathe out and turn the chest toward the bent knee, rotating from the mid-back; the ribs, then the shoulders, then the head follow.
steps.feel: a gentle wringing along the mid-back; very little in the lower back.

steps.title: Add a little more only with each in-breath
steps.action: on each in-breath lengthen again; on each out-breath turn slightly further, only if the spine stays long.
steps.feel: comfortable, 4 to 5 out of 10, no pinching.

steps.title: Turn the gaze
steps.action: gaze over the back shoulder only if the neck feels comfortable; otherwise keep the chin level, looking straight ahead.
steps.feel: a light stretch in the side of the neck, no strain.

steps.title: Hold
steps.action: stay with slow nose breaths. Beginners 5 breaths (about 30 seconds, est.); sources say about 30 seconds minimum (one snippet) and The Yoga Institute holds with the breath suspended for 6 seconds, which we do not teach.
steps.feel: slow release in the mid-back and hip; the twist deepening a tiny bit with each out-breath.
steps.breathing: slow nose breaths; count out-breaths; never hold the breath.

steps.title: Unwind slowly
steps.action: on an out-breath, turn the head back first, then the shoulders and chest, unwinding in reverse order; the hands return to the floor.
steps.feel: the spine uncoiling smoothly; no dizziness.

steps.title: Rest and switch sides
steps.action: sit tall, shake out the legs, then repeat with the left knee bent and a twist to the left.
steps.feel: both sides compared; do not force the stiffer side to match.

commonMistakes.title: Twisting from the lower back and rounding
commonMistakes.text: Twisting from the lower back and rounding. The lumbar spine rotates little, so forcing it risks the discs and joints. Fix: sit tall first, rotate from the mid-back and ribs, keep the lower back long.

commonMistakes.title: Cranking with the arm
commonMistakes.text: Cranking with the arm. Pulling hard against the knee forces a deeper twist than the spine is ready for. Fix: use the arm to lengthen up, turn only with the out-breath.

commonMistakes.title: Holding the breath
commonMistakes.text: Holding the breath. It raises effort and blood pressure. Fix: slow nose breaths; count out-breaths. Note that The Yoga Institute's version suspends the breath for 6 seconds, but we do not teach it.

commonMistakes.title: Letting a hip lift off the floor
commonMistakes.text: Letting a hip lift off the floor. The twist then comes from the pelvis, not the spine. Fix: keep both sitting bones heavy, use a blanket, or bend the lifted-side leg less.

commonMistakes.title: Slumping
commonMistakes.text: Slumping. The twist then collapses the chest. Fix: lift the chest on every in-breath; sit on a blanket.

commonMistakes.title: Cranking the neck
commonMistakes.text: Cranking the neck. Gazing over the shoulder past a comfortable range strains the neck. Fix: keep the chin level if the neck is tight.

commonMistakes.title: Forcing the bent knee across the body or pulling the planted foot
commonMistakes.text: Forcing the bent knee across the body or pulling the planted foot. It can irritate the knee or hip. Fix: keep the foot planted without twisting the knee; stop at knee pain.

commonMistakes.title: Twisting hard on a full stomach
commonMistakes.text: Twisting hard on a full stomach. The pose compresses the abdomen. Fix: practise on an empty or light stomach (several sources advise waiting a few hours after meals).

commonMistakes.title: Doing one side only or forcing the stiffer side to match
commonMistakes.text: Doing one side only or forcing the stiffer side to match. Fix: do both sides, spend about equal time, and accept differences.

commonMistakes.title: Unwinding fast
commonMistakes.text: Unwinding fast. Dizziness or a back twinge can follow. Fix: unwind head first, then shoulders, then chest, slowly.

safetyNotes: Mild twist, never pain. A gentle wringing in the mid-back and outer hip is normal; sharp pain, a pinch in the back, a pull in the knee or tingling is not.

Back and discs: several sources list recent or acute back injury, herniated disc and spinal surgery as reasons to avoid or seek professional advice (snippets). The Yoga Institute lists spinal injuries and hernia among its limitations. Sciatica sources conflict (see section 7), so ask a doctor. If cleared, keep the twist gentle and the spine long.

Osteoporosis: the 2013 International Journal of Yoga Therapy review (PubMed 24016820; snippet) concluded that spinal flexion carries the main fracture concern, though cautious guidance also warns against deep or end-range twisting. Ask a doctor; if cleared, keep rotation gentle and mid-range.

Pregnancy: The Yoga Institute and Sivananda say avoid; Do You Yoga says avoid deep closed twists that compress the abdomen; Liforme suggests an open twist away from the top leg for more room (snippets). Ask a doctor or midwife; if cleared, open twist only, small range, never compress the belly.

Recent abdominal surgery or hernia, peptic ulcer: The Yoga Institute and PharmEasy list hernia and peptic ulcer as limitations; for post-surgery and post-caesarean twisting, no source gave a fixed wait (Not found); sources agree on provider clearance first (snippets).
Blood pressure and heart: The Yoga Institute lists hypertension and cardiac ailments as limitations (snippet). Move slowly, never hold the breath, unwind slowly.
Knee and hip: keep the planted foot without twisting the knee; stop at knee pain.

Stop immediately if you feel: sharp back or neck pain, numbness or tingling down the leg or arm, dizziness, chest pain or breathlessness, a pull in the abdomen or an incision, or any pain in the knee.
Spotter: not needed. Gym etiquette: keep the mat out of walkways; do not hog the stretching area.

CYP listing: the CYP lists Vakrasana/Marichyasana; Ardha Matsyendrasana by name was not found. We present it as a close seated-twist relative and do not claim it is a CYP posture.

Hold time and breath: about 30 seconds minimum or 3-5 days a week (teaching sources) versus a 6-second breath suspension (The Yoga Institute). We chose 5 slow breaths (about 30 s, est.), no breath-holding.
Sciatica: avoid (Brett Larkin) versus helps (Lessons.com). We chose "ask a doctor; stop at leg symptoms".
Pregnancy: avoid (Yoga Institute, Sivananda) versus an open twist (Liforme, Satyori). We chose "ask a doctor; if cleared, open twist only".
Osteoporosis: flexion is the main concern; extreme twisting is also cautioned; no study shows twist fractures (Yoga U). We chose "ask a doctor; gentle mid-range only".

Not found: MDNIY technique page; confirmation of the pose in the AYUSH CYP; a pose-specific MET; measured joint-angle norms; trial evidence for this pose alone; a fixed wait for twisting after caesarean or abdominal surgery; clinical sources for cholesterol, thyroid, heart disease and surgery for this pose. Our thresholds are estimates.
Most pages were seen only as search snippets or summaries; direct page fetches were not possible.
